{"id": "e8f0fd69-5106-48e9-8a78-53e81ca53c3f", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Cross-region calls are probably part of it, but they likely don't explain a large jump on their own.

**What I found (us-east-1, account 012345678901_1, Nov 10–24)**
- Bedrock's own latency metric is flat. Nova Lite averages about 950 ms every day. Sonnet 4.5 stays around 1.1–2.6 s.
- Sonnet 5 averages about 7–9 s on most days. It spiked to about 17 s on Nov 10 and about 16 s on Nov 17. I can't tell from this data whether those spikes line up with your move.
- I didn't find any throttling or errors. I only looked at latency and invocation counts, so I didn't check those metrics directly.
- eu-west-1 has no Bedrock metrics in this account, so nothing is being served there.

**What that means**
- Bedrock's latency metric only measures time inside the service. It leaves out the network trip from your app to the endpoint. If the metric hasn't changed but your app sees slower calls, the extra time is being added outside Bedrock, which fits the cross-region path.
- Cross-region calls add one round trip per request. That's roughly 70–100 ms between Ireland and N. Virginia, which is my estimate and not something I measured. A new TCP and TLS connection costs several more round trips. If your client opens a new connection for each call, you pay that every time. This hurts most on fast, small calls like Nova Lite or embeddings, where about 1 s of model time becomes noticeably longer.
- Your models use `us.*` inference profiles. Those can route a request to other US regions, such as us-east-2 or us-west-2. A call from Europe can therefore cross the Atlantic and then be moved again inside the US. It also keeps your data in the US, which may matter after a move to eu-west-1.

**What I'd do**
1. Call Bedrock in eu-west-1 and switch to the EU inference profiles (`eu.*`) for the models that offer them. Not every model is available there, so check what eu-west-1 supports first.
2. Reuse Bedrock clients and connections instead of creating a new client per request.
3. Measure the app-side latency of the Bedrock call, split into time to first token and total time. Compare it with the metric above. The difference is your network and client overhead.

If you tell me which models matter most, I can check what's available in eu-west-1. If you give me the migration date, I can check whether the Sonnet 5 slowdowns line up with it. I can also look at the app-side side if you point me at its logs or traces.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
